parameters.content:
## 1 · Inputs

Three doors, a single pipeline. Each door stamps its `origin` field: that field decides the routing, whether the digest is sent and what is returned to the dashboard.

## 2 · Parameters

**The only node to adapt after import.**

In a container: `host.docker.internal`. On a native n8n: `127.0.0.1`. The service token lives in a *Header Auth* credential, never here.

## 3 · Control

The health pre-check separates "backend switched off" from "control crashed".

The refresh is non-blocking: if it fails, the control runs on the last known measurements.

## 4 · Reporting

All the formatting is done once in the Code node — the email nodes consume nothing but `email_subject` and `email_html`. The "no anomaly" digest is only sent on a scheduled trigger: ten clicks must not produce ten e-mails.

## 6 · Failures & response

Failures feed the alert **and** the response in parallel: the email node overwrites the JSON of the item.

The dashboard always receives a 200 — a 5xx would make it replay a control that has already run.

nodes.name: NetVerify parameters
nodes.notes: The only node to adapt after import: backend URL, recipients, sender.

nodes.name: Backend health
nodes.notes: Public route / — separates "backend switched off" from "control crashed".

nodes.name: Refresh the measurements
nodes.notes: Non-blocking. No retry: the endpoint is capped at 6 calls/hour, and insisting would burn the quota of the hourly collection.

nodes.name: Anomaly report
nodes.notes: A send failure must not invalidate a control already written to the database: the anomaly logs stay readable in the dashboard.

nodes.name: Scheduled digest?
nodes.notes: No "all clear" e-mail on a manual click: the result is already shown on screen.

assignments.name: instruction
assignments.value: The NetVerify backend is not answering. Check that the `backend` container (or `uvicorn main:app`) and PostgreSQL are started, then run the control again from the dashboard.

assignments.name: response
assignments.value: ={{ ({ status: 'error', error: { step: 'Backend health', message: ($json.error?.message || 'Backend unreachable') } }) }}

assignments.name: instruction
assignments.value: The backend answered but the analysis failed. Check the logs of the `backend` container: the error usually comes from `comparator.py` or from a database write. Do not replay blindly — a partially written control would duplicate follow-up logs.

assignments.name: response
assignments.value: ={{ ({ status: 'error', error: { step: 'D+14 compliance control', message: ($json.error?.message || 'Compliance analysis failed') } }) }}

assignments.name: step
assignments.value: Hourly collection of the NetScan measurements

assignments.name: instruction
assignments.value: The NetScan measurements were not refreshed. If the failure persists, the 06:00 D+14 control will work on stale measurements and may report anomalies that are already resolved. Check the backend, the 6 calls/hour quota and the NetScan probe.

assignments.name: origin_label
assignments.value: hourly collection of the NetScan measurements

assignments.name: response
assignments.value: ={{ ({ status: 'error', error: { step: 'Hourly collection', message: ($json.error?.message || 'Measurement refresh failed') } }) }}

nodes.name: Manual origin?
nodes.notes: "Respond to Webhook" only makes sense when the execution comes from the webhook.

nodes.name: Response to the dashboard
nodes.notes: Always 200, even on failure: a 5xx would make Streamlit replay the control directly and would duplicate the follow-up logs.

parameters.content: ## 5 · Hourly collection — refreshes the NetScan measurements every hour, so that the 06:00 control works on fresh data.
